London, 17<sup>th</sup> March 2009 



# Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest 

**Ford’s European division** said that it was adjusting production capacity to shrinking demand. The actions mainly affect Ford’s operations in Germany and Spain as well as its new Romanian manufacturing facility in Craiova.  In Spain, the Valencia plant will move to a two-shift pattern from May 1 from three shifts currently.   Currently there are no plans for forced layoffs or plant closures; talks with labor unions over the capacity reduction are ongoing.  Separately, the president of the German state of North-Rhine Westfalia, Juergen Ruettgers, announced that Ford was to invest EUR200 million at its Cologne plant. _Source:  CNN  Money_ 

**Ford,** whose Focus is the top-selling western car in Russia, cut its industry forecast for the country, saying sales may plummet as much as 50% this year in what used to be the second-fastest growing auto market.  Russian car sales in the first two months of 2009 dropped 36% to 252,314 vehicles as the ruble depreciated and interest rates rose. Russia may slide into recession this year after ten years of uninterrupted growth.  Ford stopped production at its St. Petersburg plant for one month from midDecember to mid-January.  Russia’s Economy Ministry predicts the economy will contract 2.2 % in 2009. _Source:  Bloomberg_ 

**The Obama administration** is “open minded” about giving General Motors  and Chrysler more aid and will use “all the resources” of the federal government to avoid bankruptcy, said Steven Rattner, chief adviser to the U.S. Treasury’s autos task force.  “Bankruptcy is not our goal nor a desirable outcome”. _Source:  Bloomberg_ 

**Eskom** will apply for a tariff increase “in a few weeks”, and seek a significant increase from the power regulator. 

_Source:  Engineering Weekly_ 

**At Stillwater Mining,** mine production sales totalled 133koz in Q4 08 at an overall average price of $498/oz vs.126koz at $528/oz in Q4 07. The average realised price for palladium was $368/oz (Q4 07:$389/oz). Average realised price for platinum, net of the loss on forward sales and contractual price caps, was $929/oz in Q4 08 (Q4 07:$1,006/oz).  Q4 08 revenues were $182.0 million (Q4 07:$162.4 million). Costs of metals sold for Q4 08 were $547/oz, excluding depreciation and amortization. Capex totalled another $143/oz sold. Consequently, mining operations in Q4 08 consumed around $200/oz. _Source:  Stillwater Mining_ 

**Taiwan LCD panel makers** are conservative over the order visibility in the coming quarters, despite improvements in shipments of small- to medium-size panels. Most noted that the improved shipments were caused mainly by rush orders; current shipments remain at off-season levels.  Taiwan’s economics minister contended that rush orders received by the makers recently  was a response to declining inventory, rather than a sign of a business rebound.  Taiwan LCD TV makers experienced q-o-q and y-o-y shipment declines in Q4 0

8, reflecting a weak year-end holiday shopping season. Sales of Taiwan-made LCD TVs were also affected by their less competitive pricing, as the Korean won continued to depreciate. _Source:  Digitimes_ 

**The U.S. Department of Energy’s Argonne National Laboratory** has devised a greener way to turn propane into propylene: “Using platinum clusters, we have devised a way to catalyze propane not only in a more environmentally friendly way, but also using far less energy than previous methods”. This new class of catalysts may lead to energy-efficient and environmentally friendly synthesis strategies and the possible replacement of petrochemical feedstocks by abundant small alkanes. _Source:  Argonne National Laboratory_
